newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa inches down on Azcarraga death.
newsitem.headline: Televisa inches down on Azcarraga death.

text.p: Shares listed by media group Televisa were marginally down in early trade on the Mexican bourse in response to the sudden news that former chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo had died.
Televisa CPO shares were off 50 centavos to 103.50 pesos, while the group's ADRs were unchanged at 26-3/8.
"The ADR dipped a little at the open, which was certainly on news of Azcarraga," a desk trader said.
Azcarraga Milmo, 66, known as "the Tiger", had retired for health reasons on March 4 after a quarter of a century at the helm of Televisa.

Traders said Azcarraga Milmo's death did come as a surprise. The nature of his illness was not made public until last night, when the company said Azcarraga had died of cancer. But they added that the company had already taken steps to transfer management.
When Azcarraga Milmo announced his retirement, the company said his son, Emilio Azcarraga Jean, 28, would take over as president and chief executive officer.
"Yes, Televisa is down a little, but we don't expect a massive sell-off as they have already implemented a management changeover," a Mexico City floor trader said.

"The share did take a pounding when it was originally announced Azcarraga was ill, because then there were doubts as to the company's future management. The news comes as a surprise, but they were obviously prepared for it," he added.
